chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee' from Hammad ibn Isa from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Muhrim (person in Ihram) should not answer the call of 'Labbayk' from anyone who calls him until his Ihram ends. I asked: How should he say it? He said: He should say 'O Saad'. And it is not appropriate for the Muhrim to enter the bathhouse; if he enters it, there is no penalty upon him. It was narrated.

key_terms.فَلاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ: There is no penalty/compensation upon him
key_terms.مُحْرِم: Person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.يَا سَعْدُ: A simple, non-literal response ('O Saad') used to acknowledge a call without saying 'Labbayk'
key_terms.يُلَبِّيَ: To answer the call of 'Labbayk' (responding to the invitation to perform Hajj/Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What are the rulings for a Muhrim regarding answering calls and entering the bathhouse during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the etiquette of speech during Ihram, prohibiting the recitation of the full Talbiyah ('Labbayk') in response to others to avoid ritual distraction, while permitting simple address. It further establishes the permissibility of entering a bathhouse (hammam) without penalty, reflecting the practical flexibility within the strictures of pilgrimage rites as interpreted by the Ahl al-Bayt. This ruling highlights the distinction between major ritual prohibitions and minor acts that do not break the sanctity of the state.
